correctness.rationale: For independent atomless margins, sorting X makes Y-ranks uniform π and reversing direction replaces it by π^{-1}. Lin–Han Eq.(2.4) with M=2 and self-replacement equals ξ=-2+12S/[(n+1)(4n+3)], S=two path-power min-rank edge sums plus π_{n−1}+2π_n. The edge-permutation module splits orthogonally into constants, centered vertex sums (dimension n−1), and cycle component (dimension n(n−3)/2); commutant dimension three proves irreducibility. Matrix coefficient orthogonality for π and π^{-1} gives exact covariance as squared projected inner products; explicit vertex boundary correction yields Var(S)=(n+1)(4n²+14n+35)/180 and Cov(S,S^{-1})=(4n⁴+n³+11n²−127n+147)/(18n(n−1)). Polynomial difference expansion at n=5 proves unique integer maximum. Independent exact rational enumeration of every n! permutation for n=4,5,6,7 reproduced mean, variance, inverse covariance and n=4 301/310, n=5 201/205 values. Only the algebraic proof establishes all n≥4.

originality.rationale: The new formula targets the first nontrivial two-right-neighbor Lin–Han coefficient, not the M=1 original Chatterjee statistic whose reverse covariance was published by Zhang. Zhang explicitly names M≥2 as a further problem in the material-read PDF. Lin–Han marginal moments are prior work; the exact positive reverse covariance, unique integer optimum n=5, and 10/n correlation decay are not implied by marginal variance and are supported by independent permutation enumeration and a representation-theoretic all-n proof.

value.rationale: Exact forward/reverse dependence governs finite-sample symmetrization of a widely used rank-based independence measure. Its strict positivity and maximizing n=5, with sharp n→∞ coefficient 10, resolve a specific natural statistical question not determined by marginal asymptotic normality. The result does not overclaim a joint CLT or asymptotic independence.
